customer_jl: Hey — after flipping our embeddings quant_profile to "int8-aggressive" some items in our index started returning 512-dim vectors instead of 1024. Similarity scores are all over the place. Anyone seen a dim change from quant alone? :eyes:
ashley: Ugh that sounds bad, thanks for reporting. Can you paste the exact API payload and a sample of the raw embedding vectors (first 8 numbers) + response headers?
mike: Quick note: quantization itself should not change embedding dimensionality. If dims changed something else likely changed under the hood (model variant or routing).
customer_jl: Paste below — we call the hosted endpoint like this:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/embed-large-v2","input":["doc A","doc B"],"quant_profile":"int8-aggressive","allow_fallback":true}'
```
Response headers snippet: `x-model: redwood/embed-large-v2@v3`, `x-embed-dim: 512`, `x-request-id: req_9a3f`. Response (first embedding vec): `[0.021, -0.44, 0.12, ...] (512 values)`
ashley: the `x-embed-dim: 512` is the smoking gun. If you're explicitly asking for embed-large-v2 we'd expect 1024 (our docs). Looks like the request was routed to a compact/dim-reduced variant.
customer_jl: We did set `allow_fallback=true` bc we wanted cheaper ops. Could fallback swap to a distilled/int8 compact model?
mike: Yes — routing can fallback to capacity/quant-compatible variants. However, it SHOULD preserve declared dimensionality by exposing a compatible variant. Sounds like a mapping bug: aggressive int8 selected a smaller-arch variant (512 dims) instead of the int8-quantized equivalent of embed-large-v2.
eng-ml-bot: NOTE: internal alert 0x7b3 — detected model_alias mismatch when quant_profile=int8-aggressive + allow_fallback=true. Candidate fallback: redwood/embed-large-v2-int8-compact (512d).
tim: Thanks for the logs & request id. I'm looping in eng-ml to triage — this is a serving-routing bug (quant profile -> fallback variant wrong arch). Can you also share 2 full input strings that reproduce and the full body for req_9a3f?
customer_jl: Sending two repro inputs in DM. Quick question: could client-side batching cause this? We batch many short docs together and use dynamic batching in the SDK.
ashley: Unlikely that batching would change vector length. Batching issues usually cause tokenization/truncation differences but not a change in model output dimensionality.
mike: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: set `allow_fallback=false` or pin an explicit model version that we know is 1024d (e.g., `redwood/embed-large-v2@2025-01-10`). Also set `quant_profile: "conservative"` if you need int8 speed but want safer variant mapping.
ashley: We should also ask you to check the `model_descriptor` endpoint: `GET /v1/models/redwood/embed-large-v2` — the response includes canonical dims and variant mapping. If the hosted router returns a different x-model than you requested, that's the problem.
eng-ml-bot: Action created: ML-3125 — verify fallback variant selection logic for quant_profile mappings and add a strict validation that dims stay the same for a kernel-compatible fallback.
customer_jl: Appreciate the quick triage. One more thing — we saw mild API 502s during the window, could that be related?
mike: Possibly. If primary variant was degraded the router may have triggered fallback logic more aggressively. That could explain why requests hit the compact variant intermittently. We'll correlate 502s with routing logs for req_9a3f series.
tim: Escalating to oncall eng-runtime to block problematic fallback until we patch. New action: set a temporary rule to reject fallbacks that change `embed_dim` for the same model alias.
deploy-bot: rollout-blocking-rule applied to hosted-router (temp) by tim at 2025-06-08T14:12:10Z
ashley: For customers: please pin model/version or disable fallback while we fix. We'll update this thread when ML-3125 has progress.
customer_jl: Doing that now — thanks. Will update if we see further weird dims. :thumbsup:
ashley: Closing loop here — created support ticket SUP-8821 and linked ML-3125. If you can share a sample full embedding array and request_id in SUP-8821 that helps debugging.
mike: Internal note — after patch we should add a warning to the docs about `allow_fallback` + `quant_profile` interactions until this is fixed.
customer_jl: Thanks all.
